title: You will be witnesses
src: Jesus, in the Acts of the Apostles, Acts 1:8 · World English Bible
author: Jesus, in the Acts of the Apostles
lines: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you.
You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem,
and to the uttermost parts of the earth.
why: The risen Jesus's last words in Acts, and the plan of the whole book: a ring of witnesses moving outwards from one city to the whole world. A witness does not invent a message or improve it, but says what they saw. Learn it and you carry the first Christians' sense of who they were.

title: Christ lives in me
src: Paul the Apostle, Galatians 2:20 · World English Bible
author: Paul the Apostle
lines: I have been crucified with Christ, and
it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.
That life which I now live in the flesh,
I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself up for me.
why: Paul's own summary of what happened to him: the zealous persecutor did not simply change his opinions; he says his old self died. It is one of the most personal sentences in the New Testament, and it ends not with Paul but with someone 'who loved me, and gave himself up for me'.

title: Overcome evil with good
src: Paul the Apostle, Romans 12:21 · World English Bible
author: Paul the Apostle
lines: Don’t be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
why: Eleven words that sum up how the first Christians answered a hostile world. Not 'avoid evil' or 'resist evil', but defeat it, with its opposite. Learn it for the days when someone has wronged you and every instinct says to hit back.

title: Always be ready
author: 1 Peter
lines: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts.
Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear,
Thus, while you are spoken against as evildoers, they may be disappointed who curse your good way of life in Christ.
why: Written to small, suspected communities in what is now Turkey, the same region where Pliny would soon be putting Christians on trial. It asks them to have a reason for their hope, and to give it gently, so that their lives answer the slander. It is still the best short guide to arguing for what you believe.

title: You turned to God from idols
src: Paul the Apostle, 1 Thessalonians 1:9–10 · World English Bible
author: Paul the Apostle
lines: For they themselves report concerning us what kind of a reception we had from you,
and how you turned to God from idols, to serve a living and true God,
and to wait for his Son from heaven,
whom he raised from the dead:
Jesus, who delivers us from the wrath to come.
why: From the oldest Christian writing we have, about the year 50. In one sentence Paul tells what conversion meant for a Greek in a Macedonian port: leaving the gods of the city, serving one living God, and waiting for Jesus, raised from the dead. It is the first Christian story told in a nutshell.
